title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 9° is a 'digression on group formalism', inserted into Grothendieck's long computation with the groups M_{rho,sigma}, Gamma_0 and fixed points under G (previous page). It sets up a dictionary between two kinds of data.

Situation (1). A group G, a normal subgroup 𝔊 (gothic G), and a subgroup N with phi_N: N ↪ G, such that N → G/𝔊 is surjective. Put SN = phi^{-1}(𝔊) = N ∩ 𝔊. Then N/SN ≅ G/𝔊 and G = N·𝔊.

Situation (2). The data are:
- groups 𝔊 and N;
- a normal subgroup SN of N;
- an action theta: N → Aut(𝔊);
- a homomorphism phi: SN → 𝔊.

The axioms (3) are:
- (a) for u in SN, theta(u) is conjugation by phi(u) (an inner action);
- (b) phi is N-equivariant: phi(n u n^{-1}) = theta(n)(phi(u)).

Going from (1) to (2) is immediate: theta is conjugation in G and phi is the inclusion.

The page announces the converse, carried out on the next page:
- Form the semidirect product S_0G = 𝔊 ⋊ N (written N.𝔊; the next page's 'produit direct' must mean semidirect).
- Define i: SN → S_0G by u ↦ u·phi(u)^{-1}. Axiom (a) gives u x u^{-1} = phi(u) x phi(u)^{-1}, so u commutes with phi(u). From this one checks that i is a homomorphism.
- Axiom (b) shows that N normalises i(SN), and (*) shows that i(SN) commutes with 𝔊. So i(SN) is normal.
- Then G := (𝔊 ⋊ N)/i(SN) recovers situation (1).

In modern terms, this is the standard description of a group generated by a normal subgroup and a subgroup as a quotient of their semidirect product along the antidiagonal of the intersection. Equivalently, one is pushing out the extension 1 → SN → N → N/SN → 1 along an equivariant SN → 𝔊. This is the usual way extensions of Gamma by pi with outer action are described: Schreier/Eilenberg–MacLane theory, crossed-module-type data, and pushouts of extensions as in SGA 1 / SGA 7 or in anabelian computations. It serves to describe the groups (e.g. arithmetic fundamental groups, with 𝔊 geometric and N Galois-type) in the 'équation des lacets' computations.
errors: In (1) N is required to inject into G, but in (2) phi: SN → 𝔊 is only a homomorphism. The reconstructed map N → G = (𝔊⋊N)/i(SN) has kernel ker(phi), so the two situations correspond exactly only when phi is injective (or one should allow N → G non-injective). This is a harmless generality mismatch.
On the next page S_0G = N.𝔊 is called a 'produit direct'; it must be the semidirect product 𝔊 ⋊_theta N, which is how it is used in (*).
On the next page 'N distingué dans N' should read 'SN distingué dans N'.

ideas.what: Reconstruction of a group G = N·𝔊 (𝔊 normal) from (𝔊, N, SN ⊲ N, N-action on 𝔊, equivariant SN → 𝔊 inducing inner action) as (𝔊⋊N)/{u·phi(u)^{-1}}
ideas.modern_name: quotient of semidirect product by antidiagonal; pushout of group extensions along an equivariant map (crossed-module-like data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical group theory / Schreier extension theory; folklore
ideas.where_published: pushouts of extensions appear in SGA 1 Exp. XIII-type and SGA 7 contexts; exact formulation unsure

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, standard group-theoretic lemma written out for the author's own use inside a larger computation. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Header page number reads '698' (Grothendieck's numbering); archive page number '690' at bottom left.
(1) reads 'SN = phi^{-1}(𝔊) ⊂ N' with 'd'où' above, and phi^{-1}(𝔊) written above the line; i.e. SN = N ∩ 𝔊.
(1') should be numbered '(1')' or '(1 bis)'; reads 'N --épi--> G/𝔊 i.e. N/SN ≃ G/𝔊'.
Under (2): 'SN → 𝔊, phi = phi_{SN}' is written below the line as an addition.
Last lines: 'Si comme en (1) on définit G, montrons comment un systt. (2) permet de reconstituer un systt. (1).'
